final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS-led merger with a CHF 16 billion loss ceiling, SNB CHF 100 billion liquidity facility, and Federal Council backstop for losses beyond the ceiling. The package includes a Sunday evening simultaneous announcement of the loss waterfall (AT1 written down in full first), SNB liquidity, and merger confirmation, with explicit language that unsecured creditors and deposits remain whole.
minority_objections: Wealth client demanded immediate visibility of SNB liquidity before Sunday to stop weekend deposit flight, arguing the Sunday announcement would come too late
AT1 representative insisted on precise 'written down in full prior to' language to prevent litigation, warning that ambiguous wording would trigger legal challenges Monday
key_conflicts: Tension between UBS CEO's demand for ironclad loss-ceiling protection versus Federal Council's political constraints on open-ended fiscal commitments
Conflict over timing: whether to disclose SNB liquidity immediately to stop weekend outflows versus coordinating all announcements Sunday evening
Dispute over exact statement language: AT1 rep and wealth clients demanded word-for-word precision while Council sought legally defensible but flexible wording
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to explicit language that losses beyond CHF 16 billion are borne by the Confederation without triggering resolution
UBS CEO agreed to sign merger before midnight contingent on receiving written commitments on loss ceiling and AT1 writedown language
SNB committed to unconditional CHF 100 billion facility available Monday morning regardless of asset quality deterioration
Federal Council agreed to simultaneous Sunday 19:00 announcement of all three elements (waterfall, liquidity, merger) rather than sequential disclosure
red_lines: UBS CEO: will not sign merger without explicit Federal Council guarantee that losses beyond CHF 16 billion are not UBS's problem
AT1 representative: statement must say AT1 written down 'in full prior to' any other loss absorption or litigation will follow Monday
Federal Council: will not announce open-ended deposit guarantee due to political and fiscal cost
Wealth client: will initiate Sunday wire transfers unless statement explicitly protects unsecured creditors above AT1 writedown
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The risk that weekend deposit flight would accelerate before Sunday evening announcement, despite wealth client's explicit warning that clients were moving money 'tonight'
The possibility that CHF 16 billion ceiling would be breached by Tuesday if outflows exceeded 12 billion or asset losses accelerated, acknowledged by FINMA but not fully stress-tested
The gap between legal defensibility of statement language and market comprehension—depositors 'aren't lawyers' per CS CEO but solution remained heavily focused on legal precision
downstream_risk_variables: Whether SNB liquidity visibility before Sunday could actually stop weekend outflows
Whether CHF 16 billion ceiling would hold under stress scenarios (12+ billion outflows)
Whether simultaneous Sunday 19:00 announcement would be early enough to prevent Monday market panic
Whether AT1 'written down in full' language would survive legal challenge
Whether wealth clients would actually wait for Sunday statement or initiate transfers over the weekend
uncertainty_notes: The room locked the structure (merger, loss ceiling, liquidity, Sunday announcement) but left unresolved: (1) whether the CHF 16 billion ceiling would actually hold under realistic stress, (2) whether Sunday evening timing was too late to stop weekend deposit flight already underway, and (3) whether the precise legal language would be sufficient to prevent both AT1 litigation and depositor panic. The solution assumed depositors would wait for and believe the Sunday statement, despite evidence they were moving money immediately.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB's CHF 100bn liquidity was deemed insufficient alone; required merger structure, loss ceiling, and Federal Council backstop to stabilize—drove the entire package design
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger became the core solution path; UBS CEO's three written conditions and midnight signature deadline shaped the entire negotiation and announcement structure
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council backstop for losses beyond CHF 16bn became a binding constraint—UBS would not sign without it, and it determined the Sunday statement language
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client warnings of Sunday wire transfers and 8-15bn Monday outflow projections drove the urgency for Sunday announcement and explicit unsecured creditor protection language
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 writedown 'in full prior to' became mandatory statement language and a red line for multiple parties; shaped the loss waterfall structure announced Sunday
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (AT1 vs unsecured creditors, who absorbs losses first) but did not change the outcome—waterfall was predetermined by legal hierarchy, not negotiated
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned of Monday litigation if language was ambiguous, demanded precise wording, but this refined statement language rather than changing the core decision to write down AT1
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Midnight UBS signature deadline, Sunday 19:00 announcement deadline, and 'before Monday open' framing drove the compressed timeline and forced simultaneous coordination
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Mentioned repeatedly as background threat (depositors panic, market tests the ceiling) but did not force a specific change—the Sunday timing was already locked in by other constraints
